segments.text: I've been a mechanic for 20 years and I still see mechanics wasting their time and money
with these three work lights.
Number one, the standard flashlight.
Every mechanic starts here.
It's reliable, it's simple, and it's cheap.
The problem is that it can only point in one direction.
So when you're working on a job that isn't directly in front of you, the light hits
whatever is in the way first and the thing you actually need to see is in the shadows.
It also forces you to work with one hand, or you got to hold it in your mouth,
it just isn't ideal.
Number two, the under hood bar.
You clip it to the hood, it floods the whole engine bay
and it genuinely feels like you finally solve the problem
until you need to get inside a wheel arch,
work under the dash or do anything
that isn't sitting right on top of the engine.
The bar is mounted at the hood line
and shines straight down onto the surface.
The deeper you go into the car,
the less light you have
and then you're back to squinting and guessing.
And the moment you close the hood
or move to a different part of the car,
it's completely useless.
You've spent good money on a light that only works
in one position, on one part of the car.
Number three, the headlamp.
This is what guys switch to when they want both hands free.
And I understand why, it works in theory.
But the light goes where your head goes,
not where your hands are.
When you're reaching into a tight space,
your hands are pointing one way
and your head is pointing another.
And even when you get your head in the perfect position,
your own hands are casting a shadow
directly over what you're trying to see
because the light is coming from behind you.
you're constantly adjusting your head
just to keep the light on the job
instead of having 100% focus on the work.
So what do I recommend?
This is what I use, the Antiklo Flexi Light.
It's a flexible LED light
that I can put directly into where I need light
and it illuminates everything around it.
So you're no longer pointing a light
at the problem from the outside anymore.
The light is literally right in the area which you need it.
It also means you can have both hands on the job,
giving you full focus
and saving you from a lot of frustration
that just isn't necessary.
it works perfectly with engine bays.
You can wrap it in wheel wells,
use it for under-dash electric work, et cetera.
You don't have to worry about replacing batteries
because it's rechargeable,
and it lasts seven hours on a full charge
so it easily gets you through the day.
This is by far the best light
in terms of versatility, efficiency,
and bang for your buck.
You can get them at the link below.
